title: Secret and personal-data sanitization
summary: Keeps secrets and personal data out of commits and tool output: secret scanning of added lines and masking of personal data.

questions.prompt: Are the lines a change adds scanned for secrets before a commit and a push?

options.label: A git hook and CI scan added lines for keys, tokens and labelled secrets
options.tradeoff: A pasted credential is stopped before it reaches the repository, host-independently; a rare false positive is silenced with a line marker or a path. Only added lines are read, so old history is not.

options.label: No scanning
options.tradeoff: No friction and no false positives; a committed secret is found only by the platform's own scanning or by chance.

questions.prompt: Which paths does the secret scan skip entirely? (test fixtures with fake keys, documentation of token formats)
Is personal data masked in tool output before the agent reads it?

options.label: Email addresses, card numbers and IBANs become per-session pseudonyms in tool output
options.tradeoff: The agent keeps what it needs (two addresses stay distinguishable as [email-1] and [email-2]) without seeing the data; on hosts that cannot replace tool output nothing is masked (the coverage report lists them), and prompts and file writes are never masked.

options.label: No masking
options.tradeoff: Tool output reaches the agent as it is; no pseudonym state to keep, and no chance of a masked value confusing a command.

questions.prompt: Which locale-bound types are masked as well? phone (a leading + and 8-15 digits) and national-id (US social security numbers). They match more ordinary numbers than the defaults do.
Should a call to an MCP server be refused when its arguments contain a secret?

options.label: Refuse calls carrying a secret
options.tradeoff: The pre-tool hook denies an MCP call whose input matches the shared secret patterns, naming the kind and never the text; a false positive on a token-like string blocks the call until the agent removes it.

options.label: Do not scan MCP arguments
options.tradeoff: A secret in a tool call reaches the third-party server; results are still masked where the host allows.

decisions.title: Secrets in added lines are scanned before a commit and a push
decisions.body:
## Decision

A git hook before a commit, a git hook before a push and CI scan the lines a change adds for private keys, provider tokens, JWTs and labelled secret assignments, and fail with the file, line and kind (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}). A line marked `go-getter:allow-secret` and the paths {{answer.scan-allow-paths}} are skipped.

## Why

A credential that reaches a repository must be rotated, and a pattern scan on the lines being added stops it without reading history (decision 0106).

guardrails.title: Added lines must not contain secrets

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given a committed credential must be rotated (0106), the lines a change adds must be checked for secrets before they leave the machine.

enforcement.check: No added line holds a private key, provider token, JWT or labelled secret
Never paste a credential into a file; refer to it by environment variable name

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Added lines carry no private keys, provider tokens, JWTs or `password = <value>` assignments. A false positive is marked with `go-getter:allow-secret` on its line, or its path is added to the skipped paths ({{answer.scan-allow-paths}}). A leaked secret must be rotated; deleting the commit is not enough.

decisions.title: Secrets in added lines are not scanned
decisions.body:
## Decision

No hook or CI step scans added lines for secrets (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}); `no-secrets-in-public-repo` still checks file names.

## Why

The project accepted the risk of a pasted credential for less friction (decision 0106).

decisions.title: The secret scan skips a declared list of paths
decisions.body:
## Decision

The secret scan skips the paths {{answer.scan-allow-paths}} (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}); an empty list skips none.

## Why

Fixtures and documentation hold fake keys on purpose, and a path is easier to review than a marker on every line (decision 0106).

decisions.title: Personal data in tool output is masked with per-session pseudonyms
decisions.body:
## Decision

Where the host can replace tool output, the post-tool hook replaces email addresses, payment card numbers and IBANs, and the types in [{{answer.pii-extra}}], with names such as `[email-1]`: the same value keeps its name within a session (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}). Secrets keep the single marker `[redacted by go-getter]`.

## Why

An agent that does not need personal data should not read it, and a stable name lets it tell two values apart (decision 0106).

guardrails.title: Personal data is masked in tool output

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the agent must not read personal data it does not need (0106), tool output that carries it must be masked before the agent sees it, where the host allows.

enforcement.check: The post-tool hook masks email, card numbers, IBANs and the listed types in tool output
Do not paste personal data into prompts or files; a prompt and a file write are never masked

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Tool output that carries email addresses, card numbers or IBANs (and [{{answer.pii-extra}}]) reaches the agent with each value replaced by a per-session name. Hosts that cannot replace tool output show it unmasked (the coverage report lists them); prompts and file writes are never masked, so personal data is not pasted into either.

decisions.title: Personal data in tool output is not masked
decisions.body:
## Decision

Tool output reaches the agent unmasked (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}); secrets are still redacted where restricted paths are enforced.

## Why

The project accepted the exposure for less machinery and no pseudonym state (decision 0106).

decisions.title: The locale-bound types masked in tool output are listed
decisions.body:
## Decision

The types masked in addition to email, card numbers and IBANs are [{{answer.pii-extra}}] (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}); an empty list adds none.

## Why

Phone and national-id formats are locale-bound and match ordinary numbers, so the project opts in (decision 0106).

decisions.title: MCP call arguments are scanned for secrets
decisions.body:
## Decision

A call to an MCP server whose arguments contain a secret is refused before it leaves, naming the kind of secret and never its text (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

An MCP server is third-party code; a secret in a tool call would leave the project with it (decision 0138).

guardrails.title: MCP calls carry no secret

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given an MCP server is third-party code reached with the project's context (0138), a secret in a call's arguments must be stopped by the host's hook before it leaves, since an instruction alone fails silently.

enforcement.check: The pre-tool hook denies an MCP call whose arguments contain a secret

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Do not put a secret in the arguments of an MCP tool call. The pre-tool hook denies a call whose input matches the secret patterns and names the kind; remove the value and use `go-getter secret run` or an environment variable the server reads itself. `go-getter coverage` shows the tier per host.

decisions.title: MCP call arguments are not scanned
decisions.body:
## Decision

The project does not scan the arguments of MCP calls for secrets (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The project accepted the risk for fewer blocked calls (decision 0138).
